rationale: Genome-wide Brie knockout screen (79,525 guides seen, 1,000 'Control' non-targeting) in B16-Ova-Cas9 cells, deposited as one guideCounts file per library (merged by prepare.R; guides absent from a file set to 0). Libraries: early time point; no T cells with DMSO, 5 uM (2457L) or 20 uM (2457H) Mettl3i (STM2457); OT-I co-culture at E:T 1:20 (DMSO, 5 uM), 1:5 (DMSO, 5 uM, 20 uM) and 1:1 (DMSO, 20 uM). GSM7879968's title says 20 uM but its treatment field and file name (2457L) say 5 uM; the file name is used. One library per condition. Main analysis: Mettl3i versus DMSO within co-culture, blocked by E:T ratio (each ratio has its own DMSO arm; 1:20 libraries correlate 0.90 with the matching no-T-cell library, consistent with drug-pretreated cultures split into co-culture), both doses pooled as 'M3i'; genes whose loss protects cells from T-cell killing only under Mettl3i are enriched. The paper's claim is that dsRNA sensing and interferon signalling mediate the Mettl3i-potentiated killing. Second analysis (positive-control check that T cells selected): E:T 1:5 co-culture versus no T cells, from an additive model over all ten treated libraries (~ drug + ratio, drug = DMSO or Mettl3i), so each ratio is compared with the no-T-cell libraries after adjusting for drug; Jak1, Stat1, Ifngr1/2, B2m and Tap1 are expected enriched. The 1:1 libraries are strongly bottlenecked (Spearman 0.28 between the two 1:1 arms; top 1% of guides hold 6-11% of reads).
